structured.approach: Attempt 3. Both earlier refusals were G2: the cited ap_forecast files counted as unread, even though attempt 2 re-read every one of them with Read. context_list and context_get showed that only the two contract items (feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack) can be fetched with a receipt; repository files can't. So instead of re-reading the files a third time, I re-fetched both inputs through context_get and rewrote task.repo_access in full. It cites only feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack, tool:repo-access, record:brief and record:memory, with no file: citations. I dropped details that only the repository files supported: the remote URL, the missing upstream, the reflog entries, COVERAGE_MIN and the coverage import. The step outcome rests entirely on the tool view and the inputs, so nothing essential was lost. I also left out a '[Tool result]' line that something outside my writes keeps appending to this file; my rewrite doesn't contain it.

claims.text: The Data Science lane's tasks TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) both target the ap_forecast repository.
ap_forecast is available locally, so no repository has to be created.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at d67e866, git status is clean and the agent identity has write access.
No Databricks or other workspace or database is used by ap_forecast.
ap_forecast is Python 3.9 with unittest; CI is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and enforces line coverage >= 90% plus static checks standing in for SonarQube.
The coding CI bar also requires no print, eval, exec or bare except and lines at most 140 characters.
ap_forecast is at version 0.9.0 today and TSK-03 owns its version step.
Branches are main and dev with feature branches per story; commit messages start with the story ID.
TSK-03 adds new src/ap_forecast/risk.py and tests/test_risk.py and must not change predict.py or models.json; TSK-04 changes src/ap_forecast/explain.py and tests/test_forecast.py.

open_questions: RAQ-1: feat.tasks and org.engineering_stack call for a feature branch per story, but the tool view reports one branch named feature/story. Should TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) share it? Interim: both tasks on feature/story, each commit prefixed with its story ID.
RAQ-2: No shell commands were allowed, so I couldn't check whether the CI command runs in this environment. Interim: the first CI run in DS-05/DS-06 will confirm it.
RAQ-3: Push permission to the remote wasn't tested because only the spine pushes. Write access is taken from tool:repo-access.

Process: the G2 checker doesn't count Read calls on repository files (file:<repository>/<path>), even when they were made in the same attempt. Repository-level evidence can only be cited through the tool view until this is fixed.
structured.summary: task.repo_access.md has been rewritten for attempt 3 and now cites only sources the checker accepts. The result is the same: ap_forecast is the only repository the Data Science lane needs (TSK-03, TSK-04) and it already exists, so nothing has to be created. The branch feature/story was created from dev at d67e866, git status is clean, the agent identity has write access, and no Databricks or database is used. The file also records the CI bar (at least 90% coverage plus static checks), the current version 0.9.0, and the files each task may change. Three questions remain open, none of them blocking: the branch naming, whether CI runs in this environment, and push permission. Separately, the citation checker doesn't recognise direct reads of repository files.
